title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative - Gender Transformative Joint Programme for the Promotion of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment: Towards the Elimination of Gender Based Violence

description.narrative: Outcome B: Harmful gender norms, attitudes, and behaviours are transformed at individual and community levels to prevent VAWG and advance GEWE. Under this outcome, there will be multiple social norms change strategies (e.g., community mobilisation; positive masculinities work; and whole of school approaches) are implemented at different socio-ecological levels; political party stakeholders are sensitised about negative exploitative and abusive attitudes and behaviours towards women political party candidates; Then (3) harmful social norms, attitudes and behaviours will be transformed at individual and community levels and the prevalence of violence will be reduced; Because (4) whole-of-society, evidence-based prevention initiatives can shift norms for the long term. Efforts to promote social change will build on the positive aspects, approaches and norms of the Zambian culture and traditions. Some of these include (1) the "extended family" model, which promotes social cohesiveness and respect for the elderly; (2) positive elements of the matrilineal systems within some communities that value women’s contributions and promotes them in leadership roles; (3) synchronous teachings on marriage for both men and women; and (4) the land registration system in chiefdoms. The outputs have been locally adapted and relates to outputs from the global menu focusing on community advocacy platforms are established/strengthened to develop strategies and programmes, including community dialogues, public information and advocacy campaigns, to promote gender-equitable norms, attitudes and behaviors, including in relation to women and girls’ sexuality and reproduction, self confidence and self-esteem and transforming harmful masculinities. The proposed programme strategy will harness these practices as opportunities to develop nuanced and culturally appropriate approaches to addressing GBV within communities. There are also traditional spaces that can be leveraged for promoting community dialogues around shifting harmful norms and gender action learning activities such as traditional ceremonies which have a huge following in Zambia. Programmes and activities will include building capacity of teacher educators, in service teachers, and school leadership around gender transformation of complex social norms that limit participation and retention of girls and boys in schools. There will also be strengthening existing student clubs such as gender desks/clubs and civic education as avenues; for gathering students’ input into addressing negative social norms and shaping behaviours. The outcome will also work on engagement with media networks and associations to build capacity of journalists and reporters on issues related to GEWE and GBV and the constructive and non-discriminatory narratives and discourse to be associated with these themes. These organizations and individuals will contribute significantly to the media landscape in Zambia, each playing a role in informing the public, advocating for GEWE and elimination of GBV, and ensuring the diversity of viewpoints in the media. Media enterprises are well positioned to play an advisory role in the content development and implementation plans for mass media campaigns, edutainment and related Programme interventions and activities aimed at shifting social norms including attitudes and practices that advance GEWE and help to eliminate GBV. Further the project will conduct adolescent girls’ activities at community level to build their agency & self-confidence to seek services such as FP, GBV, SRH and HIV including awareness and linkage campaigns for migrant and mobile populations to seek GBV services. These campaigns will use multiple formats such as braille, large print, sign language (where necessary) to ensure information is accessible to individuals with visual, hearing, and cognitive impairments. Information will be provided in simple, clear language with the usage of pictograms or visual aids.
